{{Short description|Terminology in physics}}

A '''power quantity''' is a power or a quantity directly proportional to [[Power (physics)|power]], e.g., [[energy density]], [[acoustic intensity]], and [[luminous intensity]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Ainslie |first=Michael A. |url=http://acousticstoday.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/A-Century-of-Sonar.pdf |title=A Century of Sonar: Planetary Oceanography, Underwater Noise Monitoring, and the Terminology of Underwater Sound |journal=Acoustics Today |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=12–19 |date=Winter 2015}}</ref>  Energy quantities may also be labelled as power quantities in this context.<ref>ISO 80000:1-2009 §&nbsp;C.3</ref>

A '''root-power quantity''' is a quantity such as [[voltage]], [[Electric current|current]], [[sound pressure]], [[electric field strength]], [[speed]], or [[charge density]], the square of which, in linear systems, is proportional to power.<ref name=Hearing>{{cite book|author=Brian C.J. Moore |title=Hearing |date=1995 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-08-053386-5 |page=11 |url={{Google books |plainurl=yes |id=OywDx9pxCMYC |page=11 }} }}</ref>  The term ''root-power quantity'' refers to the [[square root]] that relates these quantities to power. The term was introduced in {{section link|ISO 80000-1|Annex C}}; it replaces and deprecates the term "'''field quantity'''".

==Implications==
It is essential to know which category a measurement belongs to when using [[decibel]]s (dB) for comparing the [[Level (logarithmic quantity)|level]]s of such quantities.  A change of one bel in the level corresponds to a 10× change in ''power'', so when comparing power quantities ''x'' and ''y'', the difference is defined to be 10×log<sub>10</sub>(''y''/''x'') decibel.  With root-power quantities, however the difference is defined as 20×log<sub>10</sub>(''y''/''x'') dB.<ref name=Hearing/>

In the analysis of signals and systems using sinusoids, field quantities and root-power quantities may be [[complex number|complex]]-valued,<ref>ISO 80000-1:2009 §&nbsp;C.2</ref><ref>ISO 80000-3:2006 §&nbsp;0.5</ref><ref>IEC 60027-3:2002</ref>{{disputed inline|discuss=Talk:Level_(logarithmic_quantity)#"root-power_quantity"_vs._"field_quantity"|date=December 2017}} as in the [[propagation constant]].

=="Root-power quantity" vs. "field quantity"==
In justifying the deprecation of the term "field quantity" and instead using "root-power quantity" in the context of levels, ISO&nbsp;80000 draws attention to the conflicting use of the former term to mean a quantity that depends on the position,<ref>ISO 80000-1:2009 §&nbsp;C.2</ref> which in physics is called a ''[[Field (physics)|field]]''.  Such a field is often called a ''field quantity'' in the literature,{{fact|date=January 2024}} but is called a ''field'' here for clarity.  Several types of field (such as the [[electromagnetic field]]) meet the definition of a root-power quantity, whereas others (such as the [[Poynting vector]] and [[temperature]]) do not.  Conversely, not every root-power quantity is a field (such as the voltage on a [[loudspeaker]]).{{fact|date=January 2024}}
